title: Chants, Rhymes and Action Songs
introduction: Practise chants, rhymes and action songs with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: Rhymes repeat ending sounds and chants use rhythm. Actions help us enjoy and remember words.
rules: Say the original chants aloud. Tap or clap to the beat and listen for rhyming words.
Chant 1: Rain on the ground, puddles all around. Put on your boots, hear the splashing sound.
Chant 2: Fly your kite, high and bright. Watch it dance in morning light.
Chant 3: One red ball, rolling down the hall. Catch it gently, do not let it fall.
Make up a new line using a word that rhymes.
Say chants aloud with a partner, clap the beat and perform actions. Repeat the words with clear pronunciation.

examples.question: Which rhymes with ground in Chant 1?
steps: Listen to the matching ending sound.

examples.question: Which rhymes with kite in Chant 2?
steps: Kite and bright have the same ending sound.

examples.question: Which rhymes with ball in Chant 3?
Find another word that rhymes with light.
steps: Light and night share the ending sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with rain: train or leaf?
exercises.solution: Rain and train share the same -ain sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with day: play or dog?
exercises.solution: Day and play share the same long a sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with cake: lake or cup?
exercises.solution: Cake and lake share the same -ake sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with bright: night or bird?
exercises.solution: Bright and night share the same -ight sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with hall: fall or hat?
exercises.solution: Hall and fall share the same ending sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with sound: ground or green?
exercises.solution: Sound and ground share the same -ound sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with boots: roots or bed?
exercises.solution: Boots and roots share the same ending sound in the pronunciation taught here.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with tree: bee or toy?
exercises.solution: Tree and bee share the same long ee sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with red: bed or road?
exercises.solution: Red and bed share the same -ed sound.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with fish: dish or desk?
exercises.solution: Fish and dish share the same -ish sound.

exercises.question: Complete the rhyme: One, two, touch your ___. (shoe or hat)
exercises.solution: Choose the word with the same ending sound as two.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with hop: stop or run?
exercises.solution: Hop and stop share the same -op sound.

summary: Rhymes repeat ending sounds and chants use rhythm. Actions help us enjoy and remember words.
